topic.name: Finding the Existence of a Limit Using One-Sided Limits

question.explanation:
From the graph, we see that it is not possible to approach $x=-2$ from the right. Therefore, \[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \, -2^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}. \]

When we approach $x=-2$ from the left, we have \[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \, -2^{-}}f(x)=-1. \]

Since $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow -2^-} f(x) \ne \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow -2^+} f(x),$ we conclude that \[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \, -2}f(x)=\text{DNE}. \]

example.title: Identifying the Limit at an Endpoint

question.explanation:
From the graph, we see that it is not possible to approach $x=-3$ from the left. Therefore,

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-3^{-}}f(x)=\text{DNE}. \]

On the other hand, when we approach $x=-3$ from the right, we have

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-3^{+}}f(x)=2 . \]

Since $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-3^-} f(x) \ne \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-3^+} f(x),$ we conclude that \[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-3}f(x)=\text{DNE} . \]

topic.name: Finding the Existence of a Limit Using One-Sided Limits

example.title: Identifying the Limit at an Endpoint

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above?

  1. $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-2}f(x)=-2$
  2. $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,1}f(x)=\text{DNE}$
  3. $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,2}f(x)=-1$
question.explanation:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

  • Statement I is true. We see from the graph that \[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-2^-}f(x)=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-2^+}f(x)=-2. \] Therefore, $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-2}f(x)=-2.$

  • Statement II is true. Both limits $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,1^-}f(x)$ and $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,1^+}f(x)$ do not exist because the function $f(x)$ is not given in the interval $[0,2).$ Therefore,
    \[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,1}f(x)=\text{DNE}. \]

  • Statement III is false. As $x$ approaches $2$ from the left and right we get \[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,2^-}f(x)=\text{DNE}, \qquad \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,2^+}f(x)=-1. \] Therefore, $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,2^{-}}f(x)\neq \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,2^{+}}f(x).$

In conclusion, only statements I and II are true.
